source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers

coverage.scope: A. Intro §362 stay relief, statutory grounds (d)(1)-(3), burdens, timing, form of relief, other causes; B.1 §361 adequate protection foundations and §507(b); B.2 opportunity cost overview and original Problems 7.1-7.2 left unsolved

topics.title: A. Relief from the Automatic Stay: Balance, Termination and Why Creditors Move
topics.description: The secured creditor’s substantive collateral value versus bankruptcy's reorganization purpose.

entries.title: Automatic stay ends under §362(c) but relief can be ordered earlier
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: Stay's statutory duration differs by covered property and acts; property-of-estate stay ends when property leaves estate, individual-debtor protection ends under specified closing/dismissal/discharge events; secured creditors often seek earlier §362(d) relief.
entries.laymanExplanation: Filing freezes collection, not forever; a lender can ask court to let it repossess sooner.
entries.legalExplanation: Separate automatic end under §362(c) from judicial grant of §362(d) relief, and from a creditor's valid lien.
entries.examApplication: Ask date, what is stayed, whether estate holds property and whether discharge/closing/dismissal has occurred.
entries.examTrap: Do not claim all components of automatic stay end at the same moment solely because property leaves estate.

entries.title: Congress balances lien value versus breathing room for reorganization
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: Collateral value is lender's protected property interest, but immediate foreclosure may destroy going-concern value and prevent Chapter11 rehabilitation. §362(d) protects value while allowing bankruptcy time only when justified.
entries.laymanExplanation: Bank should not lose pledged property's value, but taking debtor's only truck can destroy the business.
entries.legalExplanation: Substantive value of lien protected more strongly than original nonbankruptcy foreclosure procedure.
entries.examApplication: In essay state creditor interest and reorganization purpose before statutory test.
entries.examTrap: Creditor's right to foreclose on Tuesday isn't itself unconditionally protected during stay.

entries.title: Two independent core stay-relief grounds: cause/adequate protection and absence of bankruptcy purpose
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: §362(d)(1) grants relief for cause including lack of adequate protection. §362(d)(2) grants relief as to act against property when both debtor lacks equity and property unnecessary to an effective reorganization.
entries.laymanExplanation: You can lift stay when bank's property value is threatened OR when there is no bankruptcy reason to keep property frozen.
entries.legalExplanation: Tests independent—creditor can prevail under either without also winning the other.
entries.examApplication: First test §362(d)(1); separately test both subparts of §362(d)(2).
entries.examTrap: Don't collapse lack of equity with absence of adequate protection.

entries.title: §362(d)(1) 'cause' is broader than secured creditor depreciation
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: Cause includes insufficient adequate protection but also may justify returning unrelated probate fiduciary matters, nearly completed state trials or other litigation to nonbankruptcy fora.
entries.laymanExplanation: The bankruptcy court may allow a pending lawsuit to finish in state court instead of restarting everything.
entries.legalExplanation: §1334(c)(1) abstention and comity/efficiency can support stay relief; stay may protect individual debtor even in representative capacity.
entries.examApplication: For a noncollateral motion identify prejudice, trial progress, judicial economy, estate effect.
entries.examTrap: Cause isn't limited to unpaid mortgage or secured credit.

entries.title: Chapter7 generally lacks reorganization reason to retain no-equity property
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: If collateral fully exhausts equity, trustee in liquidation ordinarily has no sale proceeds for unsecured estate; §362(d)(2)(B)'s reorganization rationale is absent, and trustee often abandons under §554.
entries.laymanExplanation: No leftover equity for estate; usually no reason to force bank to wait.
entries.legalExplanation: Statutory two-prong language remains but in Chapter7 no effective reorganization is contemplated.
entries.examApplication: Identify Chapter7 versus reorganization before analyzing necessity.
entries.examTrap: Not accurate to say a Chapter7 court can never retain encumbered asset for an estate-specific benefit.

entries.title: Chapter11: no equity by itself cannot defeat reorganization necessity
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: Where debtor has no equity, debtor can still need pledged machinery or premises to operate, preserve going-concern value and propose plausible Chapter11 plan; §362(d)(2)(B) also demands realistic feasibility.
entries.laymanExplanation: Business may be underwater yet need the property to generate revenue.
entries.legalExplanation: Both no-equity and no-necessity-for-feasible-reorganization must exist for §362(d)(2) relief.
entries.examApplication: Separate cash liquidation value from continuing operation/use and plan prospects.
entries.examTrap: No equity alone is NOT enough for §362(d)(2) in Chapter11.

entries.title: §362(d)(3) special SARE fast route
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: For claim secured by single asset real estate §101(51B), debtor must within statutory period file plan with reasonable confirmation possibility OR start qualified monthly nondefault contract-rate interest payments; otherwise stay relief follows.
entries.laymanExplanation: Single rental-building company can't sit in bankruptcy for years without filing credible plan or paying lender.
entries.legalExplanation: Source explains earliest usual day90 after filing, or 30 days after SARE determination if later, subject permissible extensions.
entries.examApplication: Identify SARE first, then dates and plan/payment alternate.
entries.examTrap: Don't apply (d)(3) automatically to every real estate debtor.

topics.title: A. §362(g), §362(e), §362(f): Burdens, Hearing Clocks and Conditional Relief
topics.description: Creditor bears debtor equity, opposing party other issues, expedited procedures.

entries.title: §362(g): only no-equity burden rests on movant
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: Movant has burden as to debtor's equity in property §362(g)(1). On all other issues—adequate protection, necessity/feasibility and SARE grounds—party opposing stay relief bears proof under §362(g)(2).
entries.laymanExplanation: Bank proves zero leftover equity; debtor must show car is protected and genuinely needed for plausible plan.
entries.legalExplanation: Burden of persuasion allocation helps when expert values ambiguous or plan unsupported.
entries.examApplication: Make a mini two-column burden chart in essay.
entries.examTrap: Not all §362(d) grounds must be affirmatively proven by creditor.

entries.title: §362(e) 30-day expiration unless court continues stay
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: For property-of-estate stay, 30 days after request court must continue stay after notice/hearing; preliminary continuation requires reasonable likelihood opponent will prevail, and final hearing usually concluded within 30 days after preliminary hearing absent agreement/compelling circumstances.
entries.laymanExplanation: Court must act quickly or frozen collateral enforcement may resume.
entries.legalExplanation: This is statutory hearing framework as described in supplied edition; actual procedural timing depends statutory provisions and context.
entries.examApplication: Write clock from motion date, distinguish preliminary versus final hearing.
entries.examTrap: Not every stay-relief motion is allowed to linger indefinitely.

entries.title: §362(e)(2) individual-case 60-day final-decision mechanism
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: For individual debtor Chapters7,11,13, source describes stay termination 60 days after request unless final court decision continuing stay; parties may agree extension or court extend for good cause.
entries.laymanExplanation: Special individual-debtor clock pushes for decision within 60 days.
entries.legalExplanation: Compare §362(e) preliminary 30-day regime and 2005 §362(e)(2), mindful of overlaps.
entries.examApplication: When debtor is person not corporation, separately check 60-day rule.
entries.examTrap: Don't apply the individual-only 60-day provision to corporation.

entries.title: §362(f) urgent ex parte relief requires irreparable harm
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: Court may grant emergency stay relief without ordinary notice if creditor demonstrates property interest will suffer irreparable damage absent immediate relief.
entries.laymanExplanation: Truck being destroyed tonight might justify quick order, not merely creditor wanting fast payment.
entries.legalExplanation: Extraordinary ex parte procedure addresses imminent loss, not routine default.
entries.examApplication: Describe specific immediate damage and inadequate normal hearings.
entries.examTrap: General inconvenience of waiting isn't necessarily irreparable harm.

entries.title: Mandatory relief if ground proven; flexible remedy form
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: §362(d) says court shall grant relief upon qualifying ground, but may terminate, annul, modify or condition stay instead of simply lifting entirely.
entries.laymanExplanation: Judge might say keep machines only if debtor pays monthly protection amount.
entries.legalExplanation: Conditioning may require payments, replacement lien or plan milestones; annulment is retroactive concept.
entries.examApplication: Propose tailored remedy and monitoring provisions.
entries.examTrap: Proving cause does not always mean immediate complete foreclosure authority.

entries.title: Denial without prejudice; changing feasibility facts support renewed motion
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: Stay relief denial at a stage of case generally isn't res judicata; lender may renew when prospects worsen or debtor makes no tangible progress.
entries.laymanExplanation: A debtor may get breathing room early, but that runs out if nothing changes.
entries.legalExplanation: Reorganization courts often indulgent in early exclusivity period, stricter later.
entries.examApplication: Specify changes in evidence and time elapsed at second motion.
entries.examTrap: Do not assume lender permanently loses chance to move again.

entries.title: Other-forum cause: state trial and fiduciary litigation
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: §362(d)(1) can allow suit to be liquidated in state court (especially trial nearly completed) and probate matters where individual debtor acts as executor not personally; court may abstain under 28 USC §1334(c)(1).
entries.laymanExplanation: If trial was one day from verdict, restarting could waste everyone's time.
entries.legalExplanation: Distinguish claim liquidation from payment out of bankruptcy estate, which still governed by claims process.
entries.examApplication: Spot case management, expertise, comity and efficiency.
entries.examTrap: Granting forum relief doesn't itself let creditor seize estate assets to collect judgment.

topics.title: B.1 Adequate Protection §361: Value Preservation, Methods, Failure
topics.description: Protection of lien-value decline, not wholesale restoration of original foreclosure rights.

entries.title: Adequate protection is temporary preservation of lien VALUE
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: Adequate protection under §361 protects a creditor's legally valid interest in estate property against decrease caused by stay/use/financing while case pending; it replaces original state-law enforcement tools with federal interim safeguards.
entries.laymanExplanation: Can't seize pledged excavator right now, but debtor must protect bank from its value falling.
entries.legalExplanation: Property rights created by nonbankruptcy law; federal bankruptcy governs interim enforcement; concept rooted in Fifth Amendment discussion plus bankruptcy policy.
entries.examApplication: Identify value at start and end, link to bankruptcy actions, then select remedy.
entries.examTrap: Do not define adequate protection as guaranteed payment of full FACE claim.

entries.title: Four interconnected Code applications
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: §363(e) may prohibit/condition use, sale or lease of collateral; §542 turnover may be ordered with protection; §362(d)(1) stay relief for inadequate protection; §364(d) priming lien demands protection of displaced lender.
entries.laymanExplanation: Estate can use machines, retrieve repossessed truck, or borrow ahead of bank only if bank's interest protected as required.
entries.legalExplanation: Each context involves same lien-value concept and distinct procedural statute.
entries.examApplication: When exam asks 'where is AP used,' name §§362,363,364,542.
entries.examTrap: §361 alone does not authorize possession or loan financing.

entries.title: Two bases: constitutional protection and statutory policy
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: Text discusses Fifth Amendment property-right concern plus Congress's policy that lender retains economic value of bargain even though procedural foreclosure timing differs; excerpt notes scholarly contest about scope of Takings Clause.
entries.laymanExplanation: Bank's pledged property has property-law significance, and Congress chose to safeguard it.
entries.legalExplanation: Court and legislation balance protection without giving lenders all state-law procedural remedies.
entries.examApplication: Explain both bases while recognizing textbook's cited critical scholarship.
entries.examTrap: Do not claim the source establishes a definitive independent constitutional minimum for every secured claim.

entries.title: §361(1) cash payments equal to threatened decrease
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: DIP or trustee can make periodic payments protecting secured interest from depreciation attributable to stay/use.
entries.laymanExplanation: If freezer equipment loses $2k/month, monthly protection may cover that loss.
entries.legalExplanation: Cash payment offsets decline rather than buying contractual rate simply because lender is delayed.
entries.examApplication: Compare actual projected monthly depreciation to promised payments.
entries.examTrap: Regular note payment amount isn't automatically proper AP amount.

entries.title: §361(2) additional or replacement liens
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: Grant creditor lien on substitute property or other collateral to compensate decrease in value of first pledged property.
entries.laymanExplanation: A bank losing truck value gets lien on other business assets worth equivalent loss.
entries.legalExplanation: Requires real value and priority of substitute lien, not merely paper promise.
entries.examApplication: On Problem7.1 test whether debtor's real estate equity may support replacement lien.
entries.examTrap: Replacement lien should not be counted twice as protectable value.

entries.title: §361(3) indubitable equivalent, not unsecured administrative rank
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: Court may give other relief ensuring indubitable equivalent of lender's protected collateral interest, e.g., financially reliable third-party guaranty; §361(3) expressly excludes ordinary §503(b)(1) administrative expense as method of AP.
entries.laymanExplanation: Bank needs truly reliable value substitute, not just 'you'll be high on the list'.
entries.legalExplanation: The alternative must protect economic equivalent and cannot merely substitute second-priority unsecured administrative expense.
entries.examApplication: Distinguish §361 present protection from §507(b) later superpriority upon failure.
entries.examTrap: Court cannot initially call §503(b)(1) priority adequate protection.

entries.title: §507(b) superpriority if protection later insufficient
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: If initially ordered AP proves inadequate and creditor suffers covered loss, §507(b) gives superpriority administrative claim for deficiency ahead of ordinary §507(a)(2) administrative claims, subject precise statutory predicates.
entries.laymanExplanation: Judge ordered $5k/month but asset depreciated more; under some circumstances bank gets special top administrative claim for uncovered loss.
entries.legalExplanation: Different from providing administrative rank upfront under prohibited §361(3); triggers when protection FAILS.
entries.examApplication: Problem7.2 asks to separate value drop, cash payments and amount left inadequately protected.
entries.examTrap: Not automatic for every decrease; must establish correct §507(b) predicates.

entries.title: Value protected against decline, not equity cushion necessarily
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: Protectable interest is lien value under §361, not the cushion itself; where value equals/surpasses debt, its preservation can be enough despite cushion shrinkage through interest accrual.
entries.laymanExplanation: Collateral can lose spare padding without bank actually losing protected $100k lien recovery.
entries.legalExplanation: Alyucan explored; Timbers discusses limits on interest/delay protection.
entries.examApplication: Compute lien recoverability separately from collateral-minus-debt margin.
entries.examTrap: Cushion disappearing doesn't mechanically prove lack of AP.

topics.title: B.2 Interim Delay, Equity Cushion and Interest: Before Alyucan and Timbers
topics.description: Distinguish loan interest from depreciation and lost foreclosure investment return.

entries.title: Equity cushion = collateral value − debt, but not same as lien value
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: Oversecured creditor has excess collateral supporting principal and potentially §506(b) interest; cushion can shrink as debt increases or property falls without automatic harm to value of currently recoverable lien.
entries.laymanExplanation: Car worth $150k and loan $100k has $50k buffer; not every buffer dollar is protected claim.
entries.legalExplanation: Alyucan rejected preservation of cushion as formula; a large cushion can nevertheless protect lien for months.
entries.examApplication: Ask whether actual recoverability drops below protected interest and whether deterioration likely.
entries.examTrap: Don't mistake mathematical cushion for standalone property right.

entries.title: Sufficient cushion can temporarily provide AP alone
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: Example in chapter: $150k collateral, $100k loan, $50k buffer; property depreciates $2k/month and debt interest accrues $1k/month, $3k/month cushion erosion; buffer lasts about seventeen months. For 12-month plan, cushion may give enough interim safety.
entries.laymanExplanation: A $50k buffer covers roughly $3k monthly deterioration for about 16.7 months.
entries.legalExplanation: Source uses an illustrative projection; value and accrual evidence can change outcome.
entries.examApplication: Estimate duration as cushion÷combined monthly adverse changes; assess plan timing.
entries.examTrap: This is a math example, not blanket rule every 17-month cushion ensures AP.

entries.title: Undersecured lost foreclosure earnings are NOT automatically AP
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: Creditor owed $100k secured by $80k may lose ability to foreclose and invest $80k during Chapter11; Timbers rejects treating forgone interest/time value as depreciation requiring payments.
entries.laymanExplanation: Bank can't demand interest just because debtor delays auction of underwater collateral.
entries.legalExplanation: §506(b) allocates postpetition interest to oversecured lenders with cushion, not undersecured lost opportunity cost.
entries.examApplication: Undersecured AP claim must show collateral decline or other real diminution, not theoretical investments.
entries.examTrap: Don't conflate §1325 plan present-value interest (later) with §361 stay-period AP.

entries.title: Single asset real estate §362(d)(3) and Chapter12 §1205 exceptions
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: Book identifies situations where Timbers no-opportunity-interest baseline differs: SARE stay retention requires timely plan or interest payments, and family-farmer §1205(b)(3) can require reasonable rent for farmland.
entries.laymanExplanation: Some specialized cases expressly demand interim payments even though ordinary AP doesn't.
entries.legalExplanation: Distinguish source of payment rule §362(d)(3) or §1205, rather than attributing to Timbers holding.
entries.examApplication: When property a rental-only building or family farm, test alternative statute.
entries.examTrap: Not correct to say Timbers means no debtor ever pays interim interest.

topics.title: B. Problems 7.1 and 7.2 — Zamboni Collateral and Failed Protection (Unsolved)
topics.description: Preserves complete multi-scenario Zamboni calculations and §507(b) analysis.

entries.title: Problem 7.1 issue checklist, no outcome
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: Analyze whether fleet is under/oversecured in alternate valuations, disputed $5k/month decline, whether $5.6k contractual payment partly interest, $200k preexisting real-property net equity, conditional cash/replacement lien under §361 and realistic reorganization necessity.
entries.laymanExplanation: What needs protecting: bank's collateral value, not necessarily its full original monthly loan payment.
entries.legalExplanation: §362(d)(1) can be cured with AP even if §362(d)(2) no equity + necessity applies differently.
entries.examApplication: Use both $425–500k and $600k scenarios, do not resolve source exercise.
entries.examTrap: Don't automatically use real estate equity for AP if senior liens or other restrictions preclude replacement lien.

entries.title: Problem 7.2 loss accounting, no answer
entries.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
entries.summary: List petition value $500k, sold value $410k, expected monthly decline $5k for ten months, actual drop $90k, ordered cash $50k; determine if initial protection failed and §507(b) entitlement from proven shortfall.
entries.laymanExplanation: Actual decline exceeded prediction; issue is whether protection gap creates statutory superpriority.
entries.legalExplanation: Identify separately payments already made, collateral sale proceeds and secured underlying claim to avoid double counting.
entries.examApplication: Show calculation framework with variables, without stating result to preserve exercise.
entries.examTrap: A simple subtraction does not alone establish §507(b) legal predicates.

problems.title: Problem 7.1 — Zamboni stay and AP
problems.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
problems.prompt: Creditor holds valid interest in business Zamboni fleet securing $500,000. Chapter11 petition collateral value RANGE $425,000–$500,000, expected depreciation $5,000/month (creditor's estimate disputed), missed monthly contract payments $5,600 of which $3,000 represents interest. DIP will keep using Zambonis. Debtor has separate real estate value $800,000 with mortgage $600,000. Creditor requests stay relief or AP. Analyze, without giving outcome. Also analyze alternative Zamboni valuation $600,000. Consider §§361,362(d)(1),(2), §506(b), value decline, equity and available substitute collateral.

problems.title: Problem 7.2 — Unexpected protection shortfall
problems.source: User-provided Tabb & Brubaker bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7, Relief from Stay and Adequate Protection, §§A–B (pasted ebook excerpt); use section and problem references, no invented page numbers
problems.prompt: Same Zamboni setting. Court fixed fleet value at $500,000 and ordered AP CASH payments $5,000 monthly. After TEN MONTHS debtor sold fleet for $410,000 and remitted proceeds to creditor. Actual collateral decline $90,000 vs expected $50,000 (ten $5,000 payments). Determine creditor rights under §507(b), allowed collateral recovery and any uncovered shortfall, leave unanswered.
